name: Super Sushi Samurai
rootCause: The new blockchain game Super Sushi Samurai, based on the Blast layer-2, was attacked due to a vulnerability in its token contract, resulting in a loss of approximately $4.6 million. Shortly after the theft, the attacker contacted the project, claiming to be a whitehat. Later, Super Sushi Samurai confirmed that the funds had been returned, minus a 5% bounty.

descriptions.text: Blast L2-based game Super Sushi Samurai's LP drained $4.8m in contract bug exploit shortly after its launch, and the price dropped 99.9%.

The new blockchain game Super Sushi Samurai, based on the Blast layer-2, was attacked due to a vulnerability in its token contract, resulting in a loss of approximately $4.6 million. Shortly after the theft, the attacker contacted the project, claiming to be a whitehat. Later, Super Sushi Samurai confirmed that the funds had been returned, minus a 5% bounty.

Super Sushi Samurai suffered an exploit on Blast in March 2024 through a flawed token transfer logic, enabling infinite balance inflation via self-transfers. The attacker drained liquidity pools for a loss of approximately $4.8 million. The defect was traceable to the contract’s handling of transfers between identical addresses. The contract's transfer logic allowed balance doubling during self-transfers by mishandling same-address transfers, resulting in infinite mint and catastrophic loss.

On March 21, 2024, the Super Sushi Samurai (SSS) token on Blast L2 was exploited for over $4.6 million. The contract's mint logic allowed attackers to multiply their balance with repeated self-transfers, collapsing liquidity and token price. The SSS token contract's mint or transfer logic failed to correctly update balances during self-transfer. When a user transferred tokens to their own address, the contract doubled their balance instead of leaving it unchanged, enabling unbounded minting and draining liquidity pools.

Super Sushi Samurai, a new blockchain game on the Blast layer-2 blockchain was exploited for $4.6 million when an attacker discovered a vulnerability in its smart contract . A bug in the mint functionality caused users who transferred their $SSS balance to themselves to receive twice as many tokens. An attacker took advantage of this to drain $4.6 million from the project, causing the $SSS token to plummet by 99%. The attacker contacted the project shortly after the theft, claiming to be a whitehat. They wrote, "Hi team, this is a whitehat rescue hack. Let's work on reimbursing the users." Super Sushi Samurai later confirmed that the funds had been returned, minus a 5% "bounty".…
